prompt: Compute the Levenshtein edit distance between two strings -- the fewest insertions, deletions, or substitutions that turn one into the other. Complete the distance method, then run the tests.
explanation: The classic solution fills an (n+1) by (m+1) table where cell [i][j] holds the distance between the first i characters of a and the first j characters of b. Row 0 and column 0 are seeded with 0,1,2,... because turning a prefix into the empty string costs one deletion per character. Every other cell is the cheapest of delete (up + 1), insert (left + 1), and substitute (diagonal + 0 or 1), so the answer ends up in the bottom-right corner.
hints: Allocate int[a.length() + 1][b.length() + 1] and fill the first row and first column with 0, 1, 2, ... first.
For cell [i][j] compare a.charAt(i - 1) with b.charAt(j - 1); matching characters cost 0, different ones cost 1.
table[i][j] = min(table[i-1][j] + 1, table[i][j-1] + 1, table[i-1][j-1] + cost), and the final answer is the last cell.
